title: Limit of a sequence

## Limit of a sequence

### Problem
Evaluate

$$\lim_{n\to\infty} \int_1^2 (\cos x)(\operatorname{Arctan} nx)\,dx,$$

where $\operatorname{Arctan}$ is the principal value arctangent function.

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
The limit is $\frac{\pi}{2}(\sin 2 - \sin 1)$.

Integrate by parts using

$$u = \operatorname{Arctan} nx, \quad du = \frac{n}{1 + n^2x^2}\,dx, \quad dv = \cos x\,dx, \quad v = \sin x$$

to get

$$\int_1^2 (\cos x)(\operatorname{Arctan} nx)\,dx = \left.(\operatorname{Arctan} nx)(\sin x)\right|_1^2 - \int_1^2 (\sin x)\frac{n}{1 + n^2x^2}\,dx$$
$$= (\operatorname{Arctan} 2n)(\sin 2) - (\operatorname{Arctan} n)(\sin 1) - \int_1^2 (\sin x)\frac{n}{1 + n^2x^2}\,dx.$$

Now

$$\left| \int_1^2 (\sin x)\frac{n}{1 + n^2x^2}\,dx \right| \le \int_1^2 |\sin x|\frac{n}{1 + n^2x^2}\,dx \le \int_1^2 \frac{n}{1 + n^2x^2}\,dx \le \int_1^2 \frac{1}{n}\,dx = \frac{1}{n} \to 0 \text{ as } n \to \infty.$$

Also,

$$\lim_{n\to\infty} \operatorname{Arctan} 2n = \lim_{n\to\infty} \operatorname{Arctan} n = \frac{\pi}{2},$$

so the desired limit is

$$\frac{\pi}{2}(\sin 2 - \sin 1).$$

### Conceptual Explanation
Integration by parts moves the limit to the boundary terms, where $\operatorname{Arctan}(kn) \to \pi/2$. The integral remainder is bounded by $\int_1^2 \frac{n}{n^2 x^2} dx = \frac{1}{2n} \to 0$.

### Key Technique
Integration by parts on oscillating/arctan factors followed by $L^1$ bounding of the derivative remainder.
